dream: I dreamed the sea went out one night and didn't come back. In the morning the ships stood on the seabed like cattle in a field, and people were walking out between them, down to towns nobody had seen in a thousand years. The lighthouses were still turning, lighting nothing. Far out, where the water had been deepest, the ground was split open, and something down there was breathing.

answer.title: The Drained Sea
answer.subtitle: as it lay on the eleventh morning after the water left
answer.premise: One night the inland sea of Aster drained away, leaving its kingdoms perched on cliffs above a white plain of salt, wrecks and drowned cities. Now everyone is walking down: to plunder, to pray, to find their dead. Far out on the seabed the Deep is breathing, and each breath is wetter than the last.

rules.name: The Draining
facts: The inland sea of Aster drained away in a single night, eleven days ago.
Nobody knows where the water went.
The seabed is a white plain of salt, wreckage and drowned towns.

rules.name: The Breathing
facts: Every few hours a warm wind rises out of the Deep, as if something below is breathing out.
Each breath is a little wetter than the last.
The salt-priests say the sea is coming back, and that it will remember who robbed it.

rules.name: Salt law
facts: Whatever is carried up the cliffs belongs to whoever carried it.
No one may bring the drowned dead up the cliffs without a salt-priest.

regions.name: The Old Coast
facts: A line of harbour cities on the cliff tops, looking down at nothing.
Its people still bless boats that will never sail again.

regions.name: Glasswold
facts: A desert of dunes fused into glass by ancient lightning.
Its caravans were the first to cross the seabed, and still are every night.

regions.name: The Seabed
facts: A plain of white salt as wide as a kingdom, strewn with wrecks.
By day it shimmers too hot to cross, so people walk it at night.

regions.name: The Field of Wrecks
facts: Where the old shipping lanes ran, a thousand ships lie on their sides in rows.
Whole families have moved into the hulls.

regions.name: Kelpreach
facts: The kelp forests lie in rotting heaps taller than houses, crawling with crabs.
The air there smells of iodine and rot.

regions.name: The Spines
facts: Sea-mountains that were reefs eleven days ago, still crusted with shell.

regions.name: The Last Orchards
facts: Terraced orchards above the old shore, the only green in sight of the seabed.
Their wells are dropping a hand's width a day.

regions.name: Cinderholm
facts: A volcanic headland whose vents hiss now that the sea no longer cools them.

places.name: Harrowgate
facts: A cliff city of lamplit terraces whose harbour now hangs forty fathoms above the seabed.
Seat of the Harbour Lords.

places.name: Tidewatch
facts: A lighthouse that still turns its lamp every night, lighting nothing.

places.name: Old Wharf
facts: The great wharf still stands on its pilings, in the air.

places.name: Cablebury
facts: Lowers people to the seabed on chains for a copper a head.

places.name: Gullhallow
facts: The gulls left with the sea; the village eats its pigeons now.

places.name: Sela
facts: The glass city, whose windows are melted dunes.
Home of the Glass Caravans.

places.name: Mirrorwell
facts: Its well water shows the sea as it was.

places.name: Dunecairn
facts: Where the caravans gather at dusk before the night walk.

places.name: Anchorfall
facts: A town built in a week out of three beached galleys.

places.name: Drownedmouth
facts: A city that sank a thousand years ago, its streets full of dead fish like spilled coins.

places.name: The Breathing Hole
facts: The edge of the Deep, where the warm wind rises.

places.name: Saltcross
facts: A crossroads of cairns where night walkers meet and trade.

places.name: The Ship Cathedral
facts: A capsized warship the salt-priests have made into a church.

places.name: Keelrow
facts: A street of hulls lived in by wreck-families.

places.name: The Admiral
facts: A flagship standing upright on its keel, untouched by salvagers.

places.name: Weedholt
facts: A fishing town that now burns dried kelp for fuel and sells the smoke as medicine.

places.name: Crabmarket
facts: Sells crabs the size of shields, caught in the kelp heaps.

places.name: Spinewatch
facts: A fort on a reef-top, held by the first company that reached it.

places.name: Shellgate
facts: The old pearl beds, now mined like silver.

places.name: Pomona
facts: The orchard capital, rich in fruit and running out of water.

places.name: Wellspring
facts: Its well is the deepest in the world and getting deeper.

places.name: The Dry Abbey
facts: Where the salt-priests train, barefoot on a floor of salt.

places.name: Cinderport
facts: A port on the outer ocean, now the only harbour that still has water.

places.name: Ashmouth
facts: Sulphur mines in the steaming vents.

features.name: The Deep
facts: A crack in the seabed a league long; no rope has found its bottom.
It breathes.

features.name: The Last Water
facts: The only water left of the sea: a warm lake that grows a little every day.

features.name: The Coral Spine
facts: A ridge of dead coral, sharp enough to cut boots.

features.name: Mount Hiss
facts: Steams day and night now the sea no longer cools it.

factions.name: The Salt-Priests
facts: They tend the drowned dead and say the sea will return.
They dress in white and walk barefoot on the salt.

factions.name: The Wreckers' Guild
facts: They claim salvage rights on every hull on the seabed.
Their marks are already painted on half the wrecks.

factions.name: The Harbour Lords
facts: The old ruling families of the coast, rich in ships that cannot sail.

factions.name: The Glass Caravans
facts: Desert traders who know how to cross open ground at night.

characters.name: Ilse Varr
facts: The lighthouse keeper's daughter who keeps the lamp at Tidewatch lit.
She believes the light is the only thing holding the sea back.

characters.name: Brother Salt
facts: The oldest salt-priest, blind, who walked out to the Deep on the first night and came back.

characters.name: Maro Dune
facts: Leader of the Glass Caravans, the first to cross the seabed and return.

characters.name: Admiral Cassa Hale
facts: She commanded the fleet that now lies in the Field of Wrecks, and refuses to leave her ship.

characters.name: Pell
facts: A boy from Anchorfall who hears words in the Deep's breathing.
